titleStmt.title: To Harriet Shaw Weaver. Saturday, 23 April 1921
titleStmt.author: James Joyce

seriesStmt.p: Machine readable texts of the unpublished correspondence of James Joyce

projectDesc.p: James Joyce's unpublished correspondence, collected, annotated, and made available as a digital edition

div.p: Many thanks for your letter with enclosed draft (£50). In my telegram of acknowledgment I asked you to send on the Times cutting (I suppose it is the article in the Literary Supplement ) mentioned in Mr Huebsch’s letter as I thought some phrases from it might be included in the prospectus which Miss Beach is having printed. I am urging this matter on because I want the advance of royalties which you are sending to be covered by subscriptions as soon as possible and before people leave their present addresses for the summer. I calculate that 250 subscriptions, chiefly on the cheapest edition ought to cover completely both your advance and the printer’s estimate. I sent you sample pages. Frankly I do not like the size of the page (which in volume form is apt to fall out of the reader’s hands when the narrative is more than usually unintelligible) but they tell me it is the usual form for such editions. Mr Huebsch’s letter confirms my opinion and I am glad I took the matter out of his hands. I am hoping that 250 names of subscribers will come in in the first month. I think I can supply 100 myself. It is very kind of you to make the proposal you did for without it I fear poor Ulysses would never reach his island home.

seg.quote: I saw Mr Pound. He has read Circe and Eumeus about which he appears to be very excited.

div.note: “Taste, Not Morals, Violated”, New York Times (23 February 1921): 12.

When plans for an American publication fell through, Sylvia Beach offered JJ to publish Ulysses in Paris. The plan was for a first edition of 1,000 copies, to be sold in advance by subscription. A four-page prospectus was mailed to several hundred people and shops in England and in France that had expressed interest and might subscribe to Ulysses. The names of the persons and shops in England were supplied to Beach by Harriet Weaver (JJ 40, 506). An image of the prospectus can be found on the website of the British Library.
On 10 April 1921, JJ wrote to Harriet Weaver about his financial straits and needing an advance on the publication of Ulysses. He asked her for help in arranging such an advance (LI 162-63).
On 17 April, JJ wrote Weaver that he had hoped to send “the first trial proofs with this letter as a curiosity” but that he had not yet received them (LI 163).
JJ had withdrawn the typescript of Ulysses from Huebsch. See JJ to Weaver, 10 April 1921.
Weaver had proposed that after the entire edition of Ulysses published by Shakespeare and Company had been sold, the Egoist Press would then publish an edition in London (JJ 505).
